queries_used.tier_2_note: Context7 and docfork were unavailable; official project documentation was verified in tier 4.

candidates.name: Vite 8
candidates.fit_for_gap: React 19 browser example and shared frontend for the Tauri example

evidence.claim: The npm registry reported Vite 8.2.0 and active maintenance.
Vite 8 documents React scaffolding and requires Node 20.19+ or 22.12+.

risks: The current example is already on Vite 8 but its full build is nondeterministic and its sibling link dependencies are not portable.
candidates.decision_rationale: Keep and harden the existing Vite app rather than replace it with a third-party starter.

candidates.name: Next.js 16 App Router
candidates.fit_for_gap: SSR, React Server Components, hydration, and client graph boundary example

evidence.claim: The npm registry reported Next.js 16.2.12, newer than the example's 16.2.1.
The App Router defines explicit Server and Client Component boundaries suitable for demonstrating server preload plus client graph hydration.
Next recommends end-to-end testing for async Server Components where unit tooling is incomplete.

risks: A global browser graph cannot be shared across server requests; the example must create request-local preload state and hydrate a client singleton.
Current remote main has a frozen-lock failure in this example.
candidates.decision_rationale: Retain the existing App Router example but make SSR/hydration the reason it exists instead of duplicating the Vite UI wholesale.

candidates.name: Official A2UI web stack (@a2ui/react + @a2ui/web_core)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Standards-compliant React rendering of agent-generated A2UI surfaces

evidence.claim: The official React renderer was published as 0.10.2 from a2ui-project/a2ui.
Official guidance says web renderers should reuse web_core for JSONL parsing, schemas, surface state, data binding, and actions instead of reimplementing roughly 3,000 lines.
The version-aware official guide labels protocol v0.9.1 current production, v0.9 previous stable, and v1.0 candidate; the 0.10.x npm distribution version is a separate version axis.

risks: The current production protocol is v0.9.1 while v1.0 is still candidate; the integration needs an explicit protocol pin and version adapter.
Pre-1.0 renderer APIs can change.
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt the maintained 0.10.x package distributions, target their documented v0.9.1/current-production protocol entry point, and keep v1.0 candidate support behind a version adapter. Prometheus should own only graph projection, transport, policy, and themed catalog integration.

candidates.name: Existing @prometheus-ags/a2ui-react alpha
candidates.fit_for_gap: Existing chat, AG-UI state projection, graph diff, and approval primitives

evidence.claim: The package consumes MESSAGE_* and STATE_* AG-UI-style events and has no A2UI surface/catalog/data-model protocol implementation.

risks: Its package name currently implies A2UI compliance that the implementation does not provide.
It duplicates chat lifecycle that KnowMe already delegates to assistant-ui.
candidates.decision_rationale: Move reusable AG-UI projection and approval behavior to an accurately named package; rebuild @prometheus-ags/a2ui-react as a thin official-A2UI integration before stable release.

candidates.name: Flutter GenUI (genui)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Standards-compliant native Flutter A2UI renderer

evidence.claim: The official Flutter repository is active and provides the maintained GenUI/A2UI implementation.
pub.dev reported genui 0.10.1 with Dart >=3.10 and Flutter >=3.35.7.
GenUI implements A2UI parsing, surface lifecycle, reactive data binding, catalogs, rendering, and user-action emission.

risks: The package is pre-1.0 and has recent breaking changes.
Its transport examples may perform networking in Dart; the imported KnowMe adapter must route actions through Riverpod to the approved transport/FFI boundary.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reuse the official protocol engine and adapt KnowMe's safe catalog/action wrapper rather than own a second Flutter protocol parser.

candidates.name: Riverpod 3 code-generation stack
candidates.fit_for_gap: Flutter normalized provider families, CRUD controllers, change invalidation, and application wiring

evidence.claim: Riverpod is the maintained reactive caching/data-binding framework selected by both existing Flutter implementations.
pub.dev reported flutter_riverpod 3.4.2 with Dart ^3.12.0.
Riverpod 3 automatically retries failed providers by default, so terminal entity/FFI errors must explicitly opt out.

risks: Latest Riverpod, Freezed, json_serializable, and analyzer versions must resolve as one tested set; the KnowMe pins document prior incompatibilities.
A stable public package should avoid a beta-only Flutter floor unless required and certified.
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt Riverpod 3, but determine a coherent generated-code toolchain from a clean stable Flutter SDK instead of independently bumping packages.

candidates.name: KnowMe prometheus_entity_management Flutter package
candidates.fit_for_gap: Riverpod 3 provider families, view descriptors, transport seam, change bridge, and optimistic CRUD

evidence.claim: The 2,704-line source package contains Riverpod 3 provider families, transport, view, sync, generated models, and CRUD, but no package-local test directory.

risks: It assumes Rust/gen_ui_core is the canonical store and is not a general drop-in Flutter graph.
The source repository has no root LICENSE file; public redistribution provenance must be resolved before copying.
The package is unpublished and uses beta Flutter/Dart floors.
candidates.decision_rationale: Import its generic provider/view/CRUD concepts with history, then decouple them from the KnowMe-specific FFI implementation behind an adapter package.

candidates.name: Existing entity_graph_flutter alpha
candidates.fit_for_gap: Dart-native normalized graph, SDL parser, transport registry, and tested cross-view behavior

evidence.claim: The 2,211-line package has graph, provider, SDL, transport, and error tests, but its manifest claims Riverpod 3 while depending on Riverpod 2.6.1.

risks: Keeping it alongside the KnowMe package would produce two canonical-store models and duplicate public APIs.
Flutter-specific dependencies are mixed with concepts that could be pure Dart.
candidates.decision_rationale: Preserve its tested graph/SDL behavior as a pure-Dart lower layer or fixture transport, then expose one Riverpod 3 public Flutter binding.

candidates.name: KnowMe gen_ui_widgets
candidates.fit_for_gap: Safe Flutter A2UI surface wrapper, content-block renderers, media resolver boundary, and shadcn-compatible UI

evidence.claim: The 2,701-line package delegates A2UI parsing/state/schema work to genui and forwards typed actions to the host, but has no package-local tests and includes broader KnowMe ContentBlock/media concerns.

risks: The A2UI wrapper and general chat ContentBlock renderer should not be forced into one public dependency.
Source licensing/provenance is unresolved.
candidates.decision_rationale: Extract the safe A2UI wrapper into a focused Flutter A2UI integration; keep or separately package generic ContentBlock widgets only if their public scope is approved.

candidates.name: KnowMe gen_ui_flutter placeholder
candidates.fit_for_gap: Potential Flutter Rust Bridge adapter package

evidence.claim: The package contains roughly 30 lines, says it is not imported by the app, and leaves generated bindings/native linking in KnowMe mobile.

risks: Moving it would create a public-looking dead package without the Rust core it describes.
candidates.decision_rationale: Do not move it as-is. Define a generic entity transport contract here; keep the KnowMe-specific FRB implementation with gen_ui_core until a genuinely reusable adapter is extracted.

candidates.name: Tauri 2 + create-tauri-app React template
candidates.fit_for_gap: One React/Vite application targeting desktop, iOS, and Android

evidence.claim: Tauri officially targets major desktop and mobile platforms.
create-tauri-app provides an officially maintained React template and pnpm workflow.
Mobile-capable plugins require explicit Android/iOS initialization, native modules when needed, permissions, and capabilities.

risks: A desktop-only Rust plugin does not become mobile-certified merely because the shell compiles.
iOS builds require macOS/Xcode and Android builds require the Android toolchain; CI must be platform-aware.
candidates.decision_rationale: Scaffold a clean universal example from the official template, then integrate the local plugin and prove each platform lane.

candidates.name: Existing @prometheus-ags/entity-graph-tauri alpha
candidates.fit_for_gap: Typed commands/events, Rust graph state, snapshot persistence, and frontend mirroring

evidence.claim: The package has TS command/event wrappers and a Rust plugin but checked-in generated bindings are currently a stub and no runnable Tauri example exists.

risks: Mobile plugin initialization, capability files, and real binding generation are not proven.
The package currently has the shared broken CommonJS configuration.
candidates.decision_rationale: Use it as the subject of the universal Tauri example, but require generated bindings and real desktop/mobile runtime tests.

candidates.name: KnowMe desktop and mobile applications
candidates.fit_for_gap: Reference implementation for React/Tauri layering, Flutter/Riverpod layering, A2UI actions, and shared domain UI

evidence.claim: KnowMe contains a production-scale React 19/Tauri desktop, Flutter/Riverpod mobile app, A2UI adapters, and entity runtime boundary patterns.

risks: The applications carry UAR, local inference, persistence, auth, product UI, and native dependencies far beyond an entity-management example.
The working tree contains unrelated user changes and a dirty submodule.
candidates.decision_rationale: Port small boundary patterns and scenario slices, not entire product directories. Never copy from the dirty working tree.

candidates.name: KnowMe Builder Flutter/A2UI templates as a migration source
candidates.fit_for_gap: Determine whether hybrid-mobile-architecture-src contains reusable Flutter/A2UI libraries to move, and reuse governed scaffolding patterns where appropriate

evidence.claim: The repository is a generator/template package, explicitly contains no runnable product application, and defines sovereign-hybrid, Flutter mobile, and Tauri desktop profiles.

Inspected Flutter material is under assets/templates/flutter-feature and assets/templates/profiles/*/mobile; no reusable top-level Flutter package/lib source exists to migrate. A2UI material is likewise template/skill guidance rather than a canonical runtime library.

risks: Moving its templates into this monorepo would create duplicate authorities and break Builder's ownership-aware upgrade model.
candidates.decision_rationale: There is no Flutter/A2UI runtime library in this repository to move. Reject it as a code-migration source while retaining a reference verdict for its templates, audits, and downstream package-consumer updates.

candidates.name: Melos 8
candidates.fit_for_gap: Dart/Flutter package discovery and workspace scripts inside the pnpm monorepo

evidence.claim: Melos 8.2.2 is maintained specifically for multi-package Dart and Flutter repositories.

risks: It adds a second workspace orchestrator; pnpm/Turbo should remain authoritative for JavaScript and Melos should be scoped to Dart only.
candidates.decision_rationale: Use Melos as a thin Dart sub-workspace runner, called from root pnpm release scripts, rather than forcing Flutter packages into Turbo.

candidates.name: assistant-ui React shell
candidates.fit_for_gap: Accessible agent thread, composer, streaming, attachments, and message actions around A2UI surfaces

evidence.claim: KnowMe already uses assistant-ui as its React chat shell while custom code handles A2UI artifacts and entity projection.

risks: It should be example-level UI infrastructure, not a required dependency of the graph or A2UI adapter package.
Current registry/repository maintenance was not checked before the research cap.
candidates.decision_rationale: Use only if Spec/Plan verifies a maintained current version. The fallback is a small accessible example-owned thread/composer shell; the official A2UI renderer and graph bridge do not depend on assistant-ui.

candidates.name: Changesets release workflow
candidates.fit_for_gap: Coordinated versioning and publication of the npm package family

evidence.claim: The action maintains a release PR and can run a repository-defined publish command.

risks: Dart and crates.io releases require separate tooling and should not be hidden behind npm Changesets state.
Fixed/linked package policy must be explicitly selected.

maintenance.last_release: Local workspace resolves @changesets/cli 2.31.0; assessment observed 2.31.1 as current on 2026-08-01

candidates.decision_rationale: Use Changesets for npm only, with a root certification command gating all ecosystems before publication.

candidates.name: Publint + Are The Types Wrong
candidates.fit_for_gap: Packed npm artifact metadata, module-format, and conditional-types certification

maintenance.last_release: Maintenance metadata not captured before the Tier 3 query cap; Publint itself executed successfully on 2026-08-01

evidence.claim: Publint validates package compatibility and already detected the shared broken CommonJS entries in this repository.
The CLI checks packed package type resolution across module modes.

candidates.decision_rationale: The checks are technically valuable and Publint found a real blocker, but final adoption remains conditional on a maintenance/version check in Spec/Plan because Analyze exhausted its registry-query budget.

candidates.name: Existing @prometheus-ags/entity-graph-a2a alpha
candidates.fit_for_gap: Deterministic reference agent endpoint, AgentCard discovery, task lifecycle, graph query/mutation parts, and artifacts for the agentic A2UI example

evidence.claim: The package implements AgentCard creation, tasks/send|get|cancel, graph mutation/query parts, in-memory task storage, and artifact responses over a Fetch-compatible server.

risks: Its self-described A2A v1.0 types were not compared with the current upstream A2A specification within the exhausted research budget.
It has no direct A2UI extension/capabilities contract, streaming task path, durable task store, or auth policy evidence in this analysis.
Its npm module output shares the release-blocking CommonJS defect.
candidates.decision_rationale: Use it as the deterministic local reference-agent base only after an upstream A2A conformance/version check. Add an A2UI artifact/metadata adapter rather than inventing a second task server.

candidates.name: Existing @prometheus-ags/entity-graph-sync with Loro + PGlite persistence
candidates.fit_for_gap: One deterministic local-first path for example and release certification

evidence.claim: The package defines SyncProvider, a graph bridge, Yjs WebSocket/WebRTC providers, and a Loro provider/channel with registry and bridge tests.
Core already exports PGlite persistence and Electric adapters, so persistence can be certified separately from peer convergence.

risks: Current Loro tests can skip when the optional dependency is unavailable, so the release job must install it and fail rather than skip.
The built-in WebSocket channel needs a real two-client convergence/reconnect test.
The sibling prometheus-entity-sync link integration is not portable and should remain an opt-in external contract job.
candidates.decision_rationale: Use PGlite for deterministic local persistence and Loro with an in-process/loopback channel for mandatory two-client convergence; add WebSocket/reconnect as an integration lane. Keep Yjs as a secondary consumer fixture, not the sole stable example path.

candidates.name: Docusaurus 3.10.2
candidates.fit_for_gap: A versioned, searchable, statically generated documentation portal deployable below the repository GitHub Pages base path

maintenance.last_release: Official installation documentation reported Docusaurus 3.10.2 on 2026-08-01

evidence.claim: Docusaurus builds static output suitable for GitHub Pages and requires all @docusaurus packages to stay on one version.
Docusaurus supports release-aware documentation routes, version selectors, banners, and bounded retained versions.
The sibling Prometheus skill-pack site supplies a proven Prometheus organization/base-path, local search, Mermaid, canonical-content, and pinned Pages workflow donor pattern.

risks: Docusaurus brings its own React build dependency and must remain isolated from the framework-neutral runtime packages.
Full version snapshots duplicate content and increase build time, so the plan should version major/minor release lines rather than every patch.
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt the current official Docusaurus line and adapt the existing Prometheus skill-pack Pages pattern, while keeping documentation dependencies in a private workspace package.

candidates.name: TypeDoc packages-mode API model
candidates.fit_for_gap: Generated, checked TypeScript API reference across the multi-package public export surface

evidence.claim: TypeDoc packages mode converts package entry points independently and merges them into one API model.
TypeDoc can discover package entry points from exports and supports explicit package-level entry point configuration.

risks: Generated API output can become noisy or drift from handwritten conceptual docs unless generation and broken-link checks are release gates.
A Docusaurus markdown integration adds a third-party plugin seam that must be pinned and smoke-tested before adoption.
candidates.decision_rationale: Use TypeDoc as the authoritative export-derived API model; adapt its output into Docusaurus only after a small proof confirms stable routes and source links.

build_required.need: A shared Project/User/Task/Activity example domain, deterministic transport fixtures, scenario IDs, and a feature-to-example coverage manifest
build_required.why_no_candidate: The value is repository-specific traceability between Prometheus public APIs and its example suite.

build_required.need: A single Flutter/Dart entity architecture combining the tested Dart graph/SDL behavior with Riverpod 3 provider families and pluggable Dart/Rust transports
build_required.why_no_candidate: The two local implementations choose incompatible canonical stores; neither is a complete general-purpose stable package as-is.

build_required.need: A Prometheus A2UI graph bridge that maps official surface data/actions to entities without owning protocol parsing or agent runtime authority
build_required.why_no_candidate: Official A2UI handles surfaces, while Prometheus-specific normalized graph projection and approval policy are unique integration concerns.

build_required.need: A deterministic reference agent for the A2UI example with no API key requirement and an optional external A2A/agent endpoint
build_required.why_no_candidate: The example must exercise Prometheus graph mutations, approvals, and protocol actions in CI; a generic demo agent cannot encode those acceptance scenarios.

build_required.need: Mobile completion of entity-graph-tauri: real generated bindings, capabilities, Android/iOS initialization where required, and desktop/mobile runtime fixtures
build_required.why_no_candidate: The plugin is repository-specific and its current Rust/TypeScript contract must be completed rather than replaced.

build_required.need: A provenance-preserving migration of reusable KnowMe Flutter sources plus license/relicensing documentation and removal of duplicate ownership
build_required.why_no_candidate: This is a source-history and governance operation across user-owned repositories, not a third-party library choice.

build_required.need: One root release certification command spanning pnpm/Turbo, Dart/Melos, Cargo, example E2E, packed consumer fixtures, skills, and registry dry runs
build_required.why_no_candidate: Existing orchestrators cover individual ecosystems; the cross-ecosystem release contract is specific to this monorepo.

build_required.need: An upstream A2A conformance/version matrix plus A2UI-over-A2A artifact/metadata adapter, streaming task scenario, and authenticated policy boundary
build_required.why_no_candidate: The existing package provides a useful custom A2A-shaped server, but its current protocol conformance and A2UI extension coverage were not established within the research cap.

build_required.need: A repository-specific documentation information architecture, Prometheus visual system, content completeness ledger, runnable-snippet verification, and release-to-docs version policy
build_required.why_no_candidate: Docusaurus and TypeDoc provide infrastructure, but the product narrative, brand implementation, coverage policy, and verified content must be designed for this package ecosystem.
